title: The messengers

visual.alt: The orange torii tunnel at Fushimi Inari in Kyoto

intro: Inari’s messengers are not dogs. Look at the ears.
task: Find a fox statue holding something. What is in its mouth?
exactLocation: Fox statues by the gates at Fushimi Inari Taisha
observeWhat: Look at the fox in front of you. What is it carrying?
hint: Look at the statues by the gates, not only on the mountain.

moreInfo.title: Kitsune
moreInfo.text: Fox spirits carry messages for Inari, kami of rice and success. A key, a jewel or a rice bale is a gift. Farmers once left the first harvest for them.

reveal: Kitsune. Fox spirits. The key, jewel or rice is a gift from Inari.

title: Who paid for a thousand gates?
intro: The mountain is striped orange because of people.
task: Write who you think paid for the gates.
hint: Read a name on the side of a gate.

storySteps.text: Walk until the gates become a tunnel.
Stop at one gate. There is a name on the wood.

choices.label: The government
choices.response: Not this mountain. The names are private.

choices.label: Families and companies
choices.response: Yes. Each gate is a donated prayer.

reveal: Ordinary people paid. The mountain is a ledger of hope, not a royal monument.

title: Bitter, then sweet
intro: Matcha was monk fuel before it was ice cream.
task: Eat or drink real matcha. Was it bitter, sweet, or both?
hint: Tea, sweets, or ice cream. Say who liked it.
reveal: The sweet exists because the tea is severe. Kyoto still serves both.

title: Has the sentence changed?
intro: You answered this in Tokyo. The artefact reads it back.
task: Has “what felt like art?” changed? Write a new sentence, or write “same”.
hint: You do not have to be clever. True is enough.
reveal: Two rooms. Two nights. The chronicle keeps both sentences.

title: What should be remembered
intro: This is not a game. Sit with what you saw.
task: Each person says one thing to remember. Write one sentence you agree on.
hint: Short is fine. True is better than complete.
reveal: Hiroshima was a city of people. Your sentence is now in the chronicle.
